en.headline: Court hears strike-out bid in Deliveroo rider’s compensation claim
en.dek: A former rider who suffered brain injuries seeks employees’ compensation, while the platform’s liquidator argues there was no employment relationship.
body: The District Court heard arguments on Tuesday over an application by Deliveroo Hong Kong’s liquidator to strike out a former rider’s claim for employees’ compensation.

The rider, identified as Lok Sze-chun, suffered severe brain injuries in a traffic accident while working for the platform. He has argued that the question of whether he was an employee at the time warrants a full trial under the Employees’ Compensation Ordinance.

Counsel for the liquidator contended that the rider offered only a bare assertion of employment status. The platform has maintained that riders operate as independent contractors under supplier agreements, with freedom to accept or reject orders.
Judge Adriana Noelle Tse Ching reserved her decision. Deliveroo exited the Hong Kong market in 2025, but the case continues as a test of gig-worker status for compensation purposes.

zh.headline: 戶戶送前外送員工傷索償案 法庭聽取剔除申請
zh.dek: 前外送員因交通意外頭部重創申請僱員補償，平台清盤人指雙方並無僱傭關係，法官押後裁決。
body: 區域法院周二就Deliveroo Hong Kong清盤人申請剔除前外送員僱員補償申索進行聴訊。
申請人駱思俊在送餐期間遭遇交通意外，頭部嚴重受傷。他根據《僱員補償條例》提出索償，認為僱傭關係問題應進行完整審訊。
清盤人一方指，申請人僅提出「赤裸斷言」，不足以支持僱員身份。平台一直主張外送員屬獨立承辦商，可自由選擇是否接單。
法官羅麗萍押後裁決。戶戶送已於2025年退出香港市場，案件仍就零工經濟下的補償問題進行審理。
